# Execution-view binding: original controls and encoding vectors

[Eight frozen mode inputs](hierarchy-mode-inputs.json) cover five valid modes
and three invalid original requests. The [captured validation](hierarchy-mode-validation.json)
compares actual owned Rust plans against `CheckedHierarchy.Modes.checkMode`:
inspection, independent root, named Fourier, generic instrument and named QPE.
All five exact comparisons pass; 2,683 individual description mutations reject
with `decodedView`. Framing and exhausted-work controls reject separately.
Independent finite-pair phase faults in the root/instrument requests and a
coordinated negative-H body/Meaning in QPE reject with the original equation
error in both inspection and comparison modes. Matching a proposed view cannot
bypass these independent obligations.

The capture test reads the same private plan allocation returned by native
checking, and the Lean runner freshly reconstructs its own original packet and
matrices. Existing hand-described vectors and independent numerical oracles
remain separate. These are curated small H, one-bit Fourier and three-qubit
QPE inputs from existing sources; generated request structure is producer
consistency evidence, not independent source or algorithm correctness. No new
source-language feature, maximum-size case, production protocol cutover, Issue
completion or constitutional guarantee is claimed. The shared native manifest
invokes `scripts/test_hierarchy_mode_views.py`, including the explicitly
selected Rust capture test; missing native configuration or zero tests fails.

[The first classical inspection refusal](first-classical-inspection-refusal.json)
preserves the first attempted classical
passthrough control and its real native refusal. Pure Meaning interfaces forbid
classical ports; this is not an accepted-but-unexecutable artifact. The hierarchy
plan regression rechecks that refusal. A separate private fault injection uses
the valid original H subject and a real fresh inspection to test retention of an
execution-preparation failure; it grants no authority to the refused artifact.

`hierarchy-plan-vectors.json` freezes four hand-described owned plans. The H
case uses an unchanged original hierarchy and independently framed bridge;
both the fresh native Rust report and Lean's original structural/finite checks
reach its exact matrix. The other three are explicitly untrusted materialization
controls for every node, literal phase, zero repeat, ordered preparation/readout
positions, reversed pack and a classical result port. They claim no accepted
instrument semantics. The first three records were fixed before either walker;
the classical-port control was appended without changing those originals.
`tests/hierarchy_execution_view.lean` checks both typed derivation and the pure
inspection comparison gate: 112 divergent descriptions reject while the original
H stays valid. Malformed framing and exhausted work also reject. The shared
native manifest retains the runner; protocol and production integration remain
pending. See the [record contract](../../../../docs/src/reference/execution-view.md#hierarchy-plan-records).

The `before/` files are exact copies of the external study made against source
`e1816954b64aaf399dc29aeb69299f14be4815a4`, before #362 implementation. The
[manifest](baseline.json) binds all 86 original files by SHA-256. The first
context, sources, commands, failed attempts and raw stdout/stderr are unchanged.
Absolute paths in observations describe the historical commands; integrity
readers never execute them.

Four original `.qli` projects cover Bell preparation/readout, HTH phase
interference, Bell partial discard and a falsely asserted unitary observing
body. The first three check/run/emit successfully; the last rejects. Three
initial direct native calls omitted the mandatory product version and reject;
appended calls using the identical packets and correct argument accept. The
16 observations retain both attempts. An independent numerical oracle agrees
with the three tiny distributions within 1e-12; this is numerical QA, not exact
source/runtime proof.

The seven Unicode artifacts have a valid H circuit-evidence positive control.
All seven original native checks accept. Rust rejects the two lone-surrogate
variants and accepts ASCII, a valid surrogate pair, its literal non-BMP spelling
and escaped/literal U+FFFD. The 14 raw observations demonstrate conservative
host refusal, not execution of a differently decoded program. Original source
text in the evidence is inert identity metadata, not a compiler-preservation
witness.

[Eighteen shared encoding vectors](canonical-vectors.json) specify QDV1 bytes
independently of either implementation. They test the primitive
[encoding contract](../../../../docs/src/reference/execution-view.md), not
complete finite/hierarchy profiles or production acceptance. This fixture
supplies no #362 completion credit, new guarantee or release approval.

## Typed finite vectors

`finite-walker-vectors.json` supplies manually specified decoded descriptions
for the three original observing roots, all 21 Raw constructors, both branch
arms, zero-width owners, distinct type trees and rectangular exact matrices.
The all-constructors row tests transport only; its concatenated operations are
not claimed to form an accepted program. Rust and Lean independently read
typed data and compare their encodings to these descriptions. The production
native protocol and acceptance authority are unchanged at this stage.

`function-cache-vectors.json` gives ten independent full function-view
expectations, including exact H–T–H coefficients, a zero-width Unit owner,
branch routes that compose or cancel, protected/certified ancilla phase,
quantum conditional phase and an adjoint dependency. Lean checks each body
freshly and derives the expected circuit; Rust checks its actual retained
circuit/matrix caches. The last row's dependency zero means the first corpus
entry. Rust maps the actual reconstructed Arc to that explicit corpus index;
this is not a claim about the enclosing native packet's entry ordering.

`finite-graph-vectors.json` gives seven complete retained-graph expectations.
Three reuse the original observing sentinels. The others distinguish Unit
interfaces, output order with a zero-width owner, declared versus derived
effects, and original evidence-table indices in a non-topological table.
Rust describes the actual graph retained by its execution handle. Lean
retains the fresh receipts from its common root check and independently
describes them; its original inspection projection preserves results, failures
and remaining work. Native comparison and the protocol cutover remain pending.

The shared Lean runner now exercises the pure finite comparison gate on these
seven independently valid originals, rejecting 71 changed candidate graph/cache
descriptions. It also checks malformed QDV1 framing, native work refusal and
original optional-request binding. Its success proof retains the original
packet and decoded root, and transports ownership/classical-scope facts from
the common checker. This gate is not yet connected to the native CLI or Rust
execution; no production protocol change or Issue completion is claimed.

The native contract adapter separately retains the typed original obligations
and fresh core results for encoded, leaf, control, control-owners, instrument
and pure-leaf requests. Universal projection equalities preserve the original
adapter computation, including errors and remaining work. The encoded/control
and instrument stage theorems bind the actual retained root/action or expected
graph. The adapter's `checkRetained_bound` also identifies every actual returned
field with the original packet, UTF-8/JSON and artifact decoding, and the exact
request-stage result with continuous work states. Its older existential
acceptance theorem alone does not supply that output-field identity.
Production contract-view comparison is still pending; these records do not
authorize execution and do not complete #362.

[Contract walker vectors](contract-walker-vectors.json) supply nine hand-specified
descriptions: seven valid original native requests cover all six obligation
kinds, and two caller circuits retain literal steps and an original-index
adjoint dependency. Rust reads actual typed obligations and caller `Circuit`
values; Lean checks the original native requests and walks their retained
stages. Every request also exercises the old/new executable projection at
normal and exhausted work budgets. Eighteen changed typed request values must
produce different descriptions; caller dependency lookup must refuse missing
or ambiguous mappings. This is walker/projection validation, not completed
production execution binding.

The [first refusal](first-contract-walker-refusal.json) preserves the original
positive-vector authoring error and native diagnostic: QIRF uses `iso`, not
`isometry`. The [second refusal](second-contract-walker-refusal.json) preserves
the subsequent invalid coefficient coordinates and independent equation
refusal. The corrected plus state uses `b = 1/2` in the existing
`a+b*sqrt(2)+i*(c+d*sqrt(2))` carrier. Neither correction changes a decoder or
acceptance rule; the original refused data remains available.
The shared Lean runner reads both records through explicit CI inputs and
freshly rechecks their distinct native invalid/equation refusals.

## Complete contract comparison

[Eight complete-contract cases](complete-contract-vectors.json) preserve graph
expectations authored before the new gate/walkers. `source_index` selects an
original request in `contract-walker-vectors.json`; only the final case replaces
its expected-artifact string with the explicit alternate reference. That
reference measures input owner8 on wire3, returns classical4 and packs Unit
owner9. Its observing meaning equals the original, while its exact decoded
identities differ. All graphs were specified independently of either walker.

The pure Lean gate describes actual and independently checked reference graphs
from one retained native-contract result, compares inside Lean, and preserves
original input/output-field binding. The runner exercises all eight positive
requests and 1,152 individual data mutations, malformed framing, exhausted work
and missing/invalid mandatory request controls. Rust independently reads actual
typed requests and retained runtime graphs, checking the same descriptions and
missing/unexpected reference rejection with a shared bounded writer. Original
caller cache/Arc aliases, hierarchy execution and production protocol cutover
remain pending. This adds no execution authority or #362 completion credit.

## Original caller alias discovery

[Caller recipes](caller-alias-recipes.json) preserve the first three expected
alias-index sequences, specified before the collector, and a fourth case for
both branch arms and certified use/logical circuits. Complete descriptions
were then authored independently of walker/native output. Rust freshly checks
the actual function receipts and original artifacts, discovers each distinct
actual Arc, and compares the complete descriptions. Equal independently checked
parents contain distinct child Arcs that the original encoder's early snapshot
deduplication does not visit. The collector must retain those children too.

The [first branch refusal](first-caller-branch-refusal.json) preserves the exact
original artifact string and actual Rust/native diagnostic. Its phi output
reused wire0; existing global wire freshness requires the corrected wire2.
The regression freshly rechecks the original `invalid_ir` refusal. This is
an input-authoring correction, not a new checker acceptance rule or a divergent
view refusal. Alias index lookup proposes a binding and cannot establish cache
equality. The shared node, byte and depth ceilings are unchanged; no maximum
quantum instance is generated.

Each recipe additionally retains a hand-authored original artifact and complete
graph, specified before the Lean caller implementation. Rust checks the exact
serialized original and actual retained graph against these expectations.
The pure Lean attachment calls the existing finite or native-contract gate
once and then compares every alias to that same fresh root's original receipt
slot. The same four bodies also exercise the contract attachment after the
explicit Bit interface and empty control-sector request are added; all six
contract kinds retain their independent request cases too. Candidate mutations
leave these independently valid original inputs fixed. Exact/one-byte-short
capacity controls check repeated-description accounting before accumulation.
The receipt-slot, comparison and inherited original-byte binding proofs are
technical staging evidence. Native CLI/Rust execution, hierarchy binding and
the protocol cutover remain pending; no new guarantee or completion is claimed.
